_note: Raw extractables. Grade affects component chain yield. Each mineral maps to a distinct component type — no ore is generically interchangeable with another. Per-Shaft abundance is set in config/profiles/*.json, not here.

minerals.name: Iron ore
minerals.description: Cut from the iron seam at the dig face. The smelter burns it with coal into steel billet.

quote.text: Heavy, rusty and everywhere. The Shaft's favourite rock, and its least favourite to carry.

minerals.usedFor: Structural repair, basic parts, tools, pipes

minerals.name: Copper ore
minerals.description: Green-streaked rock from the dig face. Drawn into copper wire at the smelter; every cable in the Shaft started as some of this.

quote.text: If it's green, it's copper. If it's moving, it's Cultivation's.

minerals.name: Coal
minerals.description: Cut at the dig face and burnt in the smelter for heat. Coked, it gives fuel for the generator and carbon for the filters.

quote.text: We dig coal to run the smelter to make the parts to fix the drill to dig more coal. It's called an economy.

minerals.usedFor: Smelting heat, and scrubber filter media
minerals._note: THE key interdependency. Doubling as activated carbon turns air quality from a fixed installation into an ongoing consumable cost, making Air permanently co-dependent on Mechanical.

minerals.name: Gold and silver ore
minerals.description: Gold and silver, weighed in kilograms rather than tonnes. The machine shop refines it into precision contacts.

quote.text: Worthless as money down here. Priceless as a contact that doesn't corrode.

minerals.usedFor: Terminals, sensors, medical equipment, the Archive

minerals.name: Limestone
minerals.description: Soft pale rock from the seams, burnt with coal into concrete for new rooms and repairs.

quote.text: The Shaft is rock we dug out and turned back into rock. Nobody finds this as funny as I do.

minerals.name: Silica sand
minerals.description: Fine sand from the seams, melted with coal into glass.

quote.text: Sand goes in, windows come out. Don't ask what we look at through them.
